claims.text: The proposed intervention changes equiatomic HfZrTi to HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9 by adding Ta, Nb, and V in a 1:1:1 ratio.
HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9 will be predominantly BCC in the as-cast condition.
HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9 will have greater tensile ductility than as-cast HfZrTi.
HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9 will have greater uniform elongation than as-cast HfZrTi.
The modification will not cause a significant loss of strength.
The modification will preserve impact-triggered energy-release characteristics.
The as-cast equiatomic HfZrTi reference alloy is single-phase HCP.
The as-cast HfZrTi reference alloy has equiaxed grains approximately 180 micrometres in size.
The HfZrTi reference alloy contains an intragranular basket-weave HCP lamellar structure.
The reference alloy was prepared from 99.95%-pure elemental feedstocks.
At x = 0.9, the alloy has a preferred <100> crystallographic orientation.
Adding Ta, Nb, and V at x = 0.9 refines the alloy's grains.
Adding Ta, Nb, and V at x = 0.9 minimizes formation of brittle omega phase.
Ta, Nb, and V act as beta/BCC stabilizers in this alloy.
Ta, Nb, and V lower the free energy of the BCC phase and suppress HCP and omega phases.
BCC stabilization, lattice distortion, and solute-dislocation interactions promote more uniform tensile plastic deformation.
More uniform tensile plastic deformation increases tensile ductility and uniform elongation while retaining sufficient strength.
Dynamic fragmentation in air promotes oxidation-based energy release.
The HfZrTi baseline may have tensile elongation around or below 5%.
The proposed behavior is expected at room temperature under quasi-static tension near 10^-3 s^-1 and under dynamic SHPB loading near 4000 s^-1 in air.

contradictions.description: The query requests an intervention for the reported HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy, but the hypothesis instead uses Ta-free equiatomic HfZrTi as its baseline and proposes HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9. Thus, the proposed base-to-modified comparison does not correspond to the requested reported baseline.
